name: Landscaping and swimming-pool services

problems.words: Gardeners skip villas and the client says nobody came for two weeks
quick_ideas: Ask teams to send a before/after photo from each visit, so every visit has proof
Spot-check a few visits against the morning list, so gaps show early.

workzap_build.text: Team check-in and check-out with location and photos for every visit, every day, with missed visits flagged.

problems.ask_first: After a visit, does the team send anything back?
problems.free_stops: Check-in method and proof rules are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare the morning route list with completed visit notes at day end, so missed villas are caught before complaints pile up.
Make one supervisor own the daily completion list in one notebook, so every skipped villa gets chased the same day.

problems.words: I can't prove the pool was cleaned on the day
quick_ideas: Ask technicians for a dated photo of each pool after service, so the visit is on record
Send the client a short visit note, so they hear it from you first.

workzap_build.text: Technicians would log tests done, equipment checks and photos on their phones, and the client would get a visit summary automatically, with no dosing guidance included.

problems.ask_first: How many pools do you service each week?
problems.free_stops: Log fields and summary format are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count completed pool visits that have a same day service note in one place, so missing proof is obvious while details are fresh.
Give one person the job of collecting each day's pool service notes into one notebook, so proof is ready when disputes start.

problems.words: Teams waste hours driving back and forth across the city
quick_ideas: Group each team's visits by area, so they stay in one zone
Put nearby clients on the same weekday, so routes repeat sensibly.

workzap_build.text: A visit schedule per client with recurring frequency, assigned team and route order for each day.

problems.ask_first: How many teams and vehicles do you have?
problems.free_stops: Routing logic is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Write each team's actual driving detours beside the planned round for a week, so wasted cross city running stands out clearly.
Give one dispatcher the weekly area plan in one notebook, so teams stop being sent back across the city.

problems.words: Pool chemicals run out quickly and I don't know where they go
quick_ideas: Record what each team is issued this week, so stock has an owner
Compare issues against visits done once, so outliers show.

workzap_build.text: A chemicals, fertiliser and parts register with issue per team and usage per site, flagged when it drifts.

problems.ask_first: How are chemicals given to teams?
problems.free_stops: Usage rules are in the solution document; dosing stays with trained technicians and product labels.

extra_ideas.text: Compare weekly stock issued to each team with visits completed that week, so unusual drawdowns stand out for checking.
Give one storekeeper one notebook for every stock issue by team and day, so each handover has a clear owner.

problems.words: Irrigation breakdowns get reported late and plants die
quick_ideas: Give clients one number for faults, so reports arrive in one place
Log each fault with date reported and fixed, so slow fixes are visible.

workzap_build.text: Irrigation and pump fault tickets from clients with response tracking across all sites.

problems.ask_first: How do clients report a broken sprinkler or pump?
problems.free_stops: Ticket flow is in the solution document; electrical work on pumps stays with a qualified electrician.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many irrigation faults sit overnight before anyone responds, so the slow handoff causing plant loss is clear.
Make one person own a single fault list checked at a fixed time daily, so breakdowns stop waiting unseen.

problems.words: Clients add things on site and refuse to pay later
quick_ideas: Get written approval with a price before any extra work, so there's a record
Keep a list of extras per project, so nothing is forgotten at billing.

workzap_build.text: A variation log on site with client approval on WhatsApp before work starts, linked to the invoice.

problems.free_stops: Approval flow is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count site extras done this week against extras written into job notes, so unpaid work leaking from jobs is visible.
Give one supervisor the job of writing every approved extra in one notebook before work starts, so billing has something to point to.

problems.words: Contracts end and we don't know until the client stops paying
quick_ideas: List every contract end date, so renewals are visible
Call clients a couple of months ahead, so you hear concerns while there's time.

workzap_build.text: A contract register with renewal alerts sent ahead of every end date.

problems.ask_first: What usually makes a client leave?
problems.free_stops: Alert timing and the renewal workflow are in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Look at which contracts end soon and have had recent complaints or missed visits, so likely losses are easier to prioritise.
Give one person one notebook of contract end months reviewed at a fixed weekly time, so renewals stop being missed.

problems.words: Communities and developers pay ninety days late
quick_ideas: List unpaid invoices by age, so the oldest are clear
Send visit proof with each invoice, so approval isn't held up.

workzap_build.text: Invoicing and receivables tracking for communities and developers with reminders on schedule.

problems.ask_first: Which type of client is slowest to pay?
problems.free_stops: Reminder schedule is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare unpaid invoices that have visit proof ready with those still missing proof, so avoidable approval delays become easier to spot.
Give one person one list of unpaid invoices reviewed at the same time each week, so follow ups stop slipping.

problems.words: Winter is dead for pools and we still carry the team
quick_ideas: List past clients who agreed to hear from you, so you have someone to offer work to
Plan one off-season service (garden, repairs, pre-season checks), so teams have work.

workzap_build.text: Seasonal offers sent from client history at the right time each year.

problems.ask_first: What do the teams do in the quiet months?
problems.free_stops: Campaign timing is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note which winter weeks had the fewest pool visits last season, so you can see the slack periods to fill.
Give one person one notebook for off season work leads from past clients, so quiet weeks have a live list to call.

problems.words: I don't know which contracts are worth keeping
quick_ideas: Compare visit time and materials against price for your largest contracts, to see the real result
Note which ones lose time to travel or extras.

workzap_build.text: Per-contract profitability from visits, materials and price, updated monthly.

problems.ask_first: Roughly how many maintenance clients do you visit each week?
problems.free_stops: Cost allocation is in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note travel time, time on site, and materials used for a few recurring contracts, so weak contracts stand out fast.
Give one person a single notebook for all extra labour and materials by contract, so renewal talks use facts not guesses.

never_say: Any fertiliser, pesticide, herbicide or pool chemical dosing, plant treatment or water-quality advice.
Any electrical advice on pumps or lighting, or structural advice on pool shells or retaining walls.
Any help billing visits not done, falsifying pool logs, dumping chemicals or green waste, or hiring without permits.
Any recording of clients' names, villa addresses, gate codes or staff names and IDs.
Anything other than emergency services first for drowning, a child alone near a pool, electric shock, chemical exposure or heatstroke.

sample_reply.person: We look after about 120 villas and clients keep saying the gardener didn't come. How do I fix this?
sample_reply.pi: Yes, this can be fixed, and you can start this week. 1) Ask each team to send a before/after photo from every visit, so each visit has proof. 2) Spot-check a few visits against the morning list, so gaps show early. Workzap can do this automatically for you: location check-ins and photos for every visit, and a visit summary sent to each client. Shall I prepare a solution document and quote for you? You're welcome to say no.
